paper_title: Direct and indirect loop equations in lattice Yang-Mills theory (Liu, 2026, JHEP)
core_reasoning_1:
\textbf{Claim.}
For the Wilson-link variation used to derive the lattice Schwinger-Dyson equations,
\[
\int DU\,\delta_\epsilon\!\left(e^{-S}W_x^{ab}(\mu,C)\right)=0
\]
implies
\[
-\left\langle W_x^{ab}(\mu,C)\,\delta_\epsilon S\right\rangle+
\left\langle\delta_\epsilon W_x^{ab}(\mu,C)\right\rangle=0.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & Z:=\displaystyle\int DU\,e^{-S}\neq 0.\\
(P2) & \displaystyle\langle X\rangle:=Z^{-1}\int DU\,e^{-S}X.\\
(P3) & \displaystyle I:=\int DU\,\delta_\epsilon\!\left(e^{-S}W_x^{ab}(\mu,C)\right)=0.\\
(P4) & \delta_\epsilon(AB)=(\delta_\epsilon A)B+A(\delta_\epsilon B).\\
(P5) & \delta_\epsilon(e^{-S})=-e^{-S}\delta_\epsilon S.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
\begin{align}
0
&=I &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=\int DU\,\delta_\epsilon\!\left(e^{-S}W_x^{ab}(\mu,C)\right) &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=\int DU\,\left[(\delta_\epsilon e^{-S})W_x^{ab}(\mu,C)+e^{-S}\delta_\epsilon W_x^{ab}(\mu,C)\right] &&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=\int DU\,e^{-S}\left[-W_x^{ab}(\mu,C)\delta_\epsilon S+\delta_\epsilon W_x^{ab}(\mu,C)\right] &&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=-\int DU\,e^{-S}W_x^{ab}(\mu,C)\delta_\epsilon S+
\int DU\,e^{-S}\delta_\epsilon W_x^{ab}(\mu,C) &&\text{linearity}\\
0
&=-Z^{-1}\int DU\,e^{-S}W_x^{ab}(\mu,C)\delta_\epsilon S+
Z^{-1}\int DU\,e^{-S}\delta_\epsilon W_x^{ab}(\mu,C) &&\text{multiply by }Z^{-1}\text{ using (P1)}\\
&=-\left\langle W_x^{ab}(\mu,C)\delta_\epsilon S\right\rangle+
\left\langle\delta_\epsilon W_x^{ab}(\mu,C)\right\rangle &&\text{by (P2).}
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[\boxed{-\left\langle W_x^{ab}(\mu,C)\,\delta_\epsilon S\right\rangle+
\left\langle\delta_\epsilon W_x^{ab}(\mu,C)\right\rangle=0}\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_3:
\textbf{Claim.}
If two SU(2) subloop cuts produce the same double-trace operator, then the corresponding paper trace relation is
\[
O_A^{\mathrm{DT}}=O_B^{\mathrm{DT}}\Longrightarrow w(O_A)+w(O_A')=w(O_B)+w(O_B').
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & O_A:=A_1A_2,
\quad O_A':=A_1\overline{A}_2.\\
(P2) & O_B:=B_1B_2,
\quad O_B':=B_1\overline{B}_2.\\
(P3) & O_A^{\mathrm{DT}}:=w(A_1)w(A_2),
\quad O_B^{\mathrm{DT}}:=w(B_1)w(B_2).\\
(P4) & w(P)w(Q)=\dfrac{1}{2}w(PQ)+\dfrac{1}{2}w(P\overline{Q})
\quad\text{for any based SU(2) loops }P,Q.\\
(P5) & O_A^{\mathrm{DT}}=O_B^{\mathrm{DT}}.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
\begin{align}
O_A^{\mathrm{DT}}
&=w(A_1)w(A_2) &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=\frac{1}{2}w(A_1A_2)+\frac{1}{2}w(A_1\overline{A}_2) &&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=\frac{1}{2}w(O_A)+\frac{1}{2}w(O_A') &&\text{by (P1)},\\
O_B^{\mathrm{DT}}
&=w(B_1)w(B_2) &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=\frac{1}{2}w(B_1B_2)+\frac{1}{2}w(B_1\overline{B}_2) &&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=\frac{1}{2}w(O_B)+\frac{1}{2}w(O_B') &&\text{by (P2)},\\
\frac{1}{2}w(O_A)+\frac{1}{2}w(O_A')
&=\frac{1}{2}w(O_B)+\frac{1}{2}w(O_B') &&\text{by (P5) and the two preceding chains}\\
w(O_A)+w(O_A')
&=w(O_B)+w(O_B') &&\text{multiply by }2.
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[\boxed{O_A^{\mathrm{DT}}=O_B^{\mathrm{DT}}\Longrightarrow w(O_A)+w(O_A')=w(O_B)+w(O_B')}\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_4:
\textbf{Claim.}
For any finite target set \(S_0\), the plaquette-cut construction exhausts the direct Schwinger-Dyson equations:
\[
\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{pc}}(S_0)=\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{dir}}^{\mathrm{SD}}(S_0).
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & S_0\text{ is a finite set of canonical Wilson loops}.\\
(P2) & \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{dir}}^{\mathrm{SD}}(S_0):=
\{E:E\text{ is an SD equation and every loop in }E\text{ lies in }S_0\}.\\
(P3) & \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{pc}}(S_0):=
\{E:E\text{ is generated by scanning }S_0\text{ for plaquette occurrences, cutting them,}\\
&\hspace{3.3cm}\text{ reconstructing the inverse variation, and retaining only equations whose loops lie in }S_0\}.\\
(P4) & E\in\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{pc}}(S_0)\Longrightarrow
E\text{ is an SD equation and every loop in }E\text{ lies in }S_0.\\
(P5) & E\in\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{dir}}^{\mathrm{SD}}(S_0)\Longrightarrow
\exists P_E\in S_0\text{ such that }P_E\text{ contains the generated plaquette of }E.\\
(P6) & P\in S_0\text{ contains a generated plaquette of }E\Longrightarrow
\text{the plaquette-cut scan of }P\text{ tests the inverse cut producing }E.\\
(P7) & A=B\Longleftrightarrow(A\subseteq B\text{ and }B\subseteq A).
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
\begin{align}
E\in\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{pc}}(S_0)
&\Longrightarrow E\text{ is an SD equation and every loop in }E\text{ lies in }S_0 &&\text{by (P4)}\\
&\Longrightarrow E\in\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{dir}}^{\mathrm{SD}}(S_0) &&\text{by (P2)},\\
\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{pc}}(S_0)
&\subseteq\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{dir}}^{\mathrm{SD}}(S_0) &&\text{from the previous implication}.
\end{align}
For the reverse inclusion, let \(E\in\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{dir}}^{\mathrm{SD}}(S_0)\) be arbitrary.
\begin{align}
E\in\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{dir}}^{\mathrm{SD}}(S_0)
&\Longrightarrow \exists P_E\in S_0\text{ containing the generated plaquette of }E &&\text{by (P5)}\\
&\Longrightarrow \text{the scan of }P_E\text{ tests the inverse cut producing }E &&\text{by (P6)}\\
&\Longrightarrow E\in\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{pc}}(S_0) &&\text{by (P3)},\\
\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{dir}}^{\mathrm{SD}}(S_0)
&\subseteq\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{pc}}(S_0) &&\text{because }E\text{ was arbitrary},\\
\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{pc}}(S_0)
&=\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{dir}}^{\mathrm{SD}}(S_0) &&\text{by (P7).}
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[\boxed{\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{pc}}(S_0)=\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{dir}}^{\mathrm{SD}}(S_0)}\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_5:
\textbf{Claim.}
For the two paper plaquette-cut examples, the twisted plaquette word yields three independent candidate SD equations, while the overlapping plaquette word yields six:
\[
W[C_1,a,b,-a,-b,a,C_2]\mapsto 3,
\qquad
W[C_1,a,b,-a,-b,a,b,-a,-b,C_2]\mapsto 6.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & Q:=a,b,-a,-b\text{ is the oriented plaquette word}.\\
(P2) & W_1:=W[C_1,a,b,-a,-b,a,C_2].\\
(P3) & W_1\text{ has }n_{1,\mathrm{cut}}=2\text{ distinct plaquette cuts}.\\
(P4) & \text{Each cut of }W_1\text{ gives }2\text{ raw backtrack insertions}.\\
(P5) & \text{Among the }W_1\text{ raw insertions, }n_{1,\mathrm{eq}}=1\text{ equivalence removes one independent candidate}.\\
(P6) & W_2:=W[C_1,a,b,-a,-b,a,b,-a,-b,C_2].\\
(P7) & W_2\text{ has }n_{2,\mathrm{cut}}=5\text{ distinct plaquette cuts}.\\
(P8) & \text{Each cut of }W_2\text{ gives }2\text{ raw backtrack insertions}.\\
(P9) & \text{Among the }W_2\text{ raw insertions, }n_{2,\mathrm{eq}}=4\text{ equivalences remove four independent candidates}.\\
(P10) & n_{\mathrm{ind}}:=n_{\mathrm{raw}}-n_{\mathrm{eq}}.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
For \(W_1\),
\begin{align}
n_{1,\mathrm{raw}}
&:=2n_{1,\mathrm{cut}} &&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=2\cdot2 &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=4,\\
n_{1,\mathrm{ind}}
&=n_{1,\mathrm{raw}}-n_{1,\mathrm{eq}} &&\text{by (P10)}\\
&=4-1 &&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=3.
\end{align}
For \(W_2\),
\begin{align}
n_{2,\mathrm{raw}}
&:=2n_{2,\mathrm{cut}} &&\text{by (P8)}\\
&=2\cdot5 &&\text{by (P7)}\\
&=10,\\
n_{2,\mathrm{ind}}
&=n_{2,\mathrm{raw}}-n_{2,\mathrm{eq}} &&\text{by (P10)}\\
&=10-4 &&\text{by (P9)}\\
&=6.
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[\boxed{W[C_1,a,b,-a,-b,a,C_2]\mapsto3,
\qquad W[C_1,a,b,-a,-b,a,b,-a,-b,C_2]\mapsto6}\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_6:
\textbf{Claim.}
The paper's loop-count ansatz gives the dimension-dependent asymptotic law
\[
N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(D)}(L)\simeq A_D L^{-(1+D/2)}(2D-1)^L,
\]
with special cases
\[
N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L)\simeq A_{2\mathrm{D}}L^{-2}3^L,
\quad
N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(3\mathrm{D})}(L)\simeq A_{3\mathrm{D}}L^{-5/2}5^L,
\quad
N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(4\mathrm{D})}(L)\simeq A_{4\mathrm{D}}L^{-3}7^L.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(D)}(L)\simeq A_D L^{-\alpha_D}\mu_D^L.\\
(P2) & \mu_D:=2D-1.\\
(P3) & \text{Closure contributes }L^{-D/2}.\\
(P4) & \text{Cyclic identification contributes }L^{-1}.\\
(P5) & L^{-\alpha_D}:=L^{-D/2}L^{-1}.\\
(P6) & D\in\{2,3,4\}.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
\begin{align}
L^{-\alpha_D}
&:=L^{-D/2}L^{-1} &&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=L^{-(D/2+1)} &&\text{law of exponents}\\
&=L^{-(1+D/2)},\\
\alpha_D
&=1+\frac{D}{2} &&\text{equate exponents},\\
N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(D)}(L)
&\simeq A_D L^{-\alpha_D}\mu_D^L &&\text{by (P1)}\\
&\simeq A_D L^{-(1+D/2)}(2D-1)^L &&\text{by (P2) and }\alpha_D=1+D/2.
\end{align}
For the three dimensions studied in the paper,
\begin{align}
D=2:\quad N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L)
&\simeq A_{2\mathrm{D}}L^{-(1+2/2)}(2\cdot2-1)^L &&\text{substitute }D=2\\
&=A_{2\mathrm{D}}L^{-2}3^L,\\
D=3:\quad N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(3\mathrm{D})}(L)
&\simeq A_{3\mathrm{D}}L^{-(1+3/2)}(2\cdot3-1)^L &&\text{substitute }D=3\\
&=A_{3\mathrm{D}}L^{-5/2}5^L,\\
D=4:\quad N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(4\mathrm{D})}(L)
&\simeq A_{4\mathrm{D}}L^{-(1+4/2)}(2\cdot4-1)^L &&\text{substitute }D=4\\
&=A_{4\mathrm{D}}L^{-3}7^L.
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[\boxed{N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(D)}(L)\simeq A_D L^{-(1+D/2)}(2D-1)^L}\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_7:
\textbf{Claim.}
For the two-dimensional loop-count ansatz, the predicted length-ratio between \(L=22\) and \(L=20\) is
\[
\frac{N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(22)}{N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(20)}=\frac{900}{121}\simeq7.438,
\]
while the table data give
\[
\frac{N_{\mathrm{data}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(22)}{N_{\mathrm{data}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(20)}=\frac{1374414}{185537}\simeq7.408.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(L)\simeq A_{2\mathrm{D}}L^{-2}3^L,
\quad A_{2\mathrm{D}}>0.\\
(P2) & N_{\mathrm{data}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(20)=185537.\\
(P3) & N_{\mathrm{data}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(22)=1374414.\\
(P4) & 3^{22}/3^{20}=3^2=9.\\
(P5) & 22^{-2}/20^{-2}=(20/22)^2=100/121.\\
(P6) & 900/121\simeq7.438.\\
(P7) & 1374414/185537\simeq7.408.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
\begin{align}
\frac{N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(22)}{N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(20)}
&\simeq \frac{A_{2\mathrm{D}}22^{-2}3^{22}}{A_{2\mathrm{D}}20^{-2}3^{20}} &&\text{by (P1)}\\
&=\frac{22^{-2}}{20^{-2}}\frac{3^{22}}{3^{20}} &&\text{cancel }A_{2\mathrm{D}}>0\\
&=\frac{100}{121}\cdot9 &&\text{by (P4), (P5)}\\
&=\frac{900}{121} &&\text{multiply}\\
&\simeq7.438 &&\text{by (P6)},\\
\frac{N_{\mathrm{data}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(22)}{N_{\mathrm{data}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(20)}
&=\frac{1374414}{185537} &&\text{by (P2), (P3)}\\
&\simeq7.408 &&\text{by (P7).}
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[\boxed{\frac{N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(22)}{N_{\mathrm{loop}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(20)}=\frac{900}{121}\simeq7.438,
\quad
\frac{N_{\mathrm{data}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(22)}{N_{\mathrm{data}}^{(2\mathrm{D})}(20)}\simeq7.408}\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_9:
\textbf{Claim.}
For loop equations partitioned into target variables \(\mathbf{x}\) and leaked auxiliary variables \(\mathbf{z}\),
\[
A\mathbf{x}+B\mathbf{z}=0,
\]
any row-combination vector \(u\) satisfying \(u^TB=0\) induces the indirect target-space equation
\[
u^TA\mathbf{x}=0.
\]
For the paper's toy system \(x-y=z\) and \(x+y=2z\), this elimination gives \(x=3y\).

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & A\mathbf{x}+B\mathbf{z}=0.\\
(P2) & u^TB=0.\\
(P3) & u^T(A\mathbf{x}+B\mathbf{z})=u^TA\mathbf{x}+u^TB\mathbf{z}.\\
(P4) & x-y=z.\\
(P5) & x+y=2z.\\
(P6) & x,y,z\text{ are scalar variables}.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
\begin{align}
A\mathbf{x}+B\mathbf{z}
&=0 &&\text{by (P1)}\\
u^T(A\mathbf{x}+B\mathbf{z})
&=u^T0 &&\text{left multiply by }u^T\\
u^TA\mathbf{x}+u^TB\mathbf{z}
&=0 &&\text{by (P3)}\\
u^TA\mathbf{x}+0\mathbf{z}
&=0 &&\text{by (P2)}\\
u^TA\mathbf{x}
&=0.
\end{align}
For the scalar toy system,
\begin{align}
2(x-y)
&=2z &&\text{multiply (P4) by }2\\
x+y
&=2(x-y) &&\text{substitute (P5)}\\
x+y
&=2x-2y &&\text{distribute}\\
3y
&=x &&\text{subtract }x\text{ and add }2y\\
x
&=3y &&\text{symmetry of equality.}
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[\boxed{u^TB=0\Longrightarrow u^TA\mathbf{x}=0,
\qquad (x-y=z\text{ and }x+y=2z)\Longrightarrow x=3y}\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_10:
\textbf{Claim.}
For the two-dimensional truncated basis \(S^{[12]}\), projection from higher-length auxiliary spaces yields exactly two indirect constraints, reducing the direct count of independent target variables from \(68\) to \(66\):
\[
n_{\mathrm{indirect}}(S^{[12]})=2,
\qquad d_{\mathrm{direct}}=68,
\qquad d_{\mathrm{projected}}=66.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & |S^{[12]}|=119.\\
(P2) & r_{\mathrm{direct}}(S^{[12]}):=51.\\
(P3) & r_{\mathrm{proj}}(S^{[12]}\leftarrow S^{[14]}):=53.\\
(P4) & r_{\mathrm{proj}}(S^{[12]}\leftarrow S^{[16]}):=53.\\
(P5) & r_{\mathrm{proj}}(S^{[12]}\leftarrow S^{[18]}):=53.\\
(P6) & n_{\mathrm{indirect}}:=r_{\mathrm{proj}}-r_{\mathrm{direct}}.\\
(P7) & d:=|S^{[12]}|-r\text{ for a rank }r\text{ system of independent linear constraints on }S^{[12]}.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
\begin{align}
r_{\mathrm{proj}}
&:=r_{\mathrm{proj}}(S^{[12]}\leftarrow S^{[18]}) &&\text{choose the largest listed auxiliary space}\\
&=53 &&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=r_{\mathrm{proj}}(S^{[12]}\leftarrow S^{[16]}) &&\text{by (P4), (P5)}\\
&=r_{\mathrm{proj}}(S^{[12]}\leftarrow S^{[14]}) &&\text{by (P3), (P4)},\\
n_{\mathrm{indirect}}
&:=r_{\mathrm{proj}}-r_{\mathrm{direct}} &&\text{by (P6)}\\
&=53-51 &&\text{by (P2) and }r_{\mathrm{proj}}=53\\
&=2,\\
d_{\mathrm{direct}}
&:=|S^{[12]}|-r_{\mathrm{direct}} &&\text{by (P7)}\\
&=119-51 &&\text{by (P1), (P2)}\\
&=68,\\
d_{\mathrm{projected}}
&:=|S^{[12]}|-r_{\mathrm{proj}} &&\text{by (P7)}\\
&=119-53 &&\text{by (P1) and }r_{\mathrm{proj}}=53\\
&=66.
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[\boxed{n_{\mathrm{indirect}}(S^{[12]})=2,
\qquad d_{\mathrm{direct}}=68,
\qquad d_{\mathrm{projected}}=66}\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_11:
\textbf{Claim.}
For the first two-dimensional indirect equation, if the six enlarged \(S^{[14]}\) equations in the paper are decomposed into target parts \(T_i\) and length-14 auxiliary parts \(Z_i\), then the coefficient vector
\[
c=(1,-1,1,-1,1,-1)
\]
eliminates all length-14 variables and gives the projected relation
\[
\mathcal{I}_{5.2}:=T_1-T_2+T_3-T_4+T_5-T_6=0.
\]

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & E_i:=T_i+Z_i=0\quad\text{for }i=1,2,3,4,5,6.\\
(P2) & T_i\text{ contains only loops of length }\leq12.\\
(P3) & Z_i\text{ contains only length-14 auxiliary loops}.\\
(P4) & c:=(c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4,c_5,c_6):=(1,-1,1,-1,1,-1).\\
(P5) & \displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{6}c_iZ_i=0.\\
(P6) & \displaystyle\mathcal{I}_{5.2}:=\sum_{i=1}^{6}c_iT_i.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
\begin{align}
0
&=\sum_{i=1}^{6}c_iE_i &&\text{because }E_i=0\text{ by (P1)}\\
&=\sum_{i=1}^{6}c_i(T_i+Z_i) &&\text{substitute (P1)}\\
&=\sum_{i=1}^{6}c_iT_i+\sum_{i=1}^{6}c_iZ_i &&\text{linearity}\\
&=\sum_{i=1}^{6}c_iT_i+0 &&\text{by (P5)}\\
&=\mathcal{I}_{5.2} &&\text{by (P6)},\\
\mathcal{I}_{5.2}
&=\sum_{i=1}^{6}c_iT_i &&\text{by (P6)}\\
&=T_1-T_2+T_3-T_4+T_5-T_6 &&\text{by (P4)}.
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[\boxed{\mathcal{I}_{5.2}=T_1-T_2+T_3-T_4+T_5-T_6=0}\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
core_reasoning_12:
\textbf{Claim.}
For the vertex-structure filtering tests reported in the paper, cases I and II retain all projected equations while reducing the enlarged loop sets by
\[
1-\frac{79884}{121223}\simeq0.341
\quad\text{and}\quad
1-\frac{38322}{225570}\simeq0.830,
\]
respectively.

\textbf{Premises.}
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
(P1) & \text{Case I: }n_{\mathrm{SDE}}=121223,
\quad n_{\mathrm{filter}}=79884,
\quad r_{\mathrm{SDE}}=2586,
\quad r_{\mathrm{filter}}=2586.\\
(P2) & \text{Case II: }m_{\mathrm{SDE}}=225570,
\quad m_{\mathrm{filter}}=38322,
\quad s_{\mathrm{SDE}}=347,
\quad s_{\mathrm{filter}}=347.\\
(P3) & \rho_{\mathrm{red}}:=1-n_{\mathrm{filter}}/n_{\mathrm{SDE}}\text{ for a loop-set reduction fraction}.\\
(P4) & \rho_{\mathrm{ret}}:=r_{\mathrm{filter}}/r_{\mathrm{SDE}}\text{ for an equation-retention fraction}.\\
(P5) & 1-79884/121223\simeq0.341.\\
(P6) & 1-38322/225570\simeq0.830.
\end{array}
\]

\textbf{Derivation.}
For case I,
\begin{align}
\rho_{\mathrm{red}}^{\mathrm{I}}
&:=1-\frac{n_{\mathrm{filter}}}{n_{\mathrm{SDE}}} &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=1-\frac{79884}{121223} &&\text{by (P1)}\\
&\simeq0.341 &&\text{by (P5)},\\
\rho_{\mathrm{ret}}^{\mathrm{I}}
&:=\frac{r_{\mathrm{filter}}}{r_{\mathrm{SDE}}} &&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=\frac{2586}{2586} &&\text{by (P1)}\\
&=1.
\end{align}
For case II,
\begin{align}
\rho_{\mathrm{red}}^{\mathrm{II}}
&:=1-\frac{m_{\mathrm{filter}}}{m_{\mathrm{SDE}}} &&\text{by (P3)}\\
&=1-\frac{38322}{225570} &&\text{by (P2)}\\
&\simeq0.830 &&\text{by (P6)},\\
\rho_{\mathrm{ret}}^{\mathrm{II}}
&:=\frac{s_{\mathrm{filter}}}{s_{\mathrm{SDE}}} &&\text{by (P4)}\\
&=\frac{347}{347} &&\text{by (P2)}\\
&=1.
\end{align}

\textbf{Final Result.}
\[\boxed{\rho_{\mathrm{red}}^{\mathrm{I}}\simeq0.341,
\quad \rho_{\mathrm{ret}}^{\mathrm{I}}=1,
\quad \rho_{\mathrm{red}}^{\mathrm{II}}\simeq0.830,
\quad \rho_{\mathrm{ret}}^{\mathrm{II}}=1}\]
\hfill$\blacksquare$
